text:
maria: Heads-up — after landing the kernel-selector change last night, canaries show ~+18% GPU memory use on inference workers serving prefix/prompt-cache heavy traffic. Happening on both 80B and 70B variants. Profiling attached below (short).

jon: Can you paste the quick nvidia-smi/pmap output? Is it steady growth or instant bump on task start?

maria: quick snippet from canary 3 (repro):
```bash
# repro snippet
./run_infer --model redwood-70b --prefix-ttl 14400 --batch=auto --canary=true
# sample watch
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv -l 1
```
Observations: memory jumps ~2.2GB at workload start, then drifts up ~200-300MB over 20m. Heap/profile shows extra transient buffers not being freed until GC/compaction.

perf-bot: quick-profile: kernel-selector=v2-dyn, batch-heuristic=adaptive, workspace-pool=disabled, kv-shards=16, prefix-ttl=4h
- peak_rss_delta: +18%
- live_allocations: +1.9M frames
- fragmentation_index: 0.27

kai: My hunch: new kernel selection chooses a dynamic algo that allocates per-invocation temp buffers sized to worst-case block, and because workspace-pool was off, those buffers get carved from the general allocator and create fragmentation (slabs leaking small free holes). Also the prefix cache's shard compaction path isn't triggering because TTL is long, so shards keep growing.

sophie: Repro steps + logs look good. I can repro locally with a synthetic mix (long prefix + random batch sizes). I see repeated allocations around 64-256KB that never coalesce.

jon: Short mitigation plan: 1) flip workspace-pool=enabled (reuse buffers) in canary; 2) reduce default prefix TTL from 4h -> 30m for canaries to force compaction; 3) add short-lived periodic slab compaction after X allocations. Can we try 1+2 first?

maria: I'm rolling canary with workspace-pool=enabled + TTL=30m to 10% of traffic now. Patch: revert flag for kernel-selector available if needed.

kai: Also add a quick instrument: track per-shard "allocated_bytes" over time and expose on the Console so we can A/B hit-rate vs mem. If kernel path is the root cause, the revert should drop the bump immediately.

perf-bot: canary-run-1942: results after 12m
- mem_peak_delta: -12% vs bad canary
- latency_p95: +0.4% (noise)
- kv_shard_hitrate: stable (slight -0.5%)

sophie: Nice. Can we snapshot a heap profile for one of the affected workers and run the allocator analyzer? I captured a heap (link in the thread) and ran a quick diff — a lot of 128KB arenas held by the allocator's free-lists.

maria: Decision: roll TTL change to prod for all prefix-heavy routes, enable workspace pooling globally for next deploy. I'll open a follow-up for deeper allocator work (defrag/coalescing + periodic sweep) and the kernel-selector opt-in toggle for safer rollouts. Ticket: INFR-3245.

jon: I'll add the per-shard metric to the Console dashboard and create a short alert if allocated_bytes/shard > threshold for 10m.

kai: For follow-up RFC: propose a coalescing freelist, plus a gentle background compaction that runs at low GPU utilization. Will draft and ping for review.

maria: Thanks all — keeping an eye on canary. If anyone sees regressions in p95, ping here and I'll rollback the kernel change. :thumbsup:
